2026-11-02.meal: Veggie fajitas (plus a fajita bowl for Jess's lunch tomorrow)
2026-11-02.note: Moved from Sunday. Make one extra portion for Jess's work lunch on Tuesday as a fajita bowl.

ingredients: 1 microwave rice pouch (for the lunch bowl)
To serve: salsa, soured cream, lettuce, avocado
steps: Fry the onions and peppers in the oil for 8–10 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the beans, sweetcorn and a splash of water. Take out Mathilda's portion now, keeping it plain.
Stir the fajita seasoning through the rest and simmer for 5 minutes.
Spoon one portion into a lunch box for tomorrow and let it cool.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or the microwave. Fill with the filling, cheese and toppings, fold and serve.

For the lunch bowl: once cool, put the rice pouch (unopened) and the filling in the fridge. At work, microwave the filling until piping hot, heat the rice, and top with cheese, lettuce, salsa and a dollop of soured cream (pack the cold toppings in a separate pot).
recipe.tip: Mathilda: keep hers mild with no seasoning. Cool the lunch portion within an hour and keep it in the fridge overnight.

2026-11-03.meal: Slow-cooker sausage & bean casserole with mash (half saved for Thursday)
2026-11-03.note: This week's one meat night, for Jess and Frank. Put it on before work and leave it on low all day. A normal batch does 2 portions tonight and 2 for Thursday. Hull hockey training 6–7pm (Hymers College).

ingredients: 400g tin cannellini or butter beans, drained
Mash (fresh potatoes or microwave pouches) or crusty bread, to serve
steps: In the morning, brown the sausages in the oil in a frying pan for 5 minutes (skip this if you're short on time, it's just for colour), then put them in the slow cooker.
Soften the onion in the same pan for 5 minutes, add the garlic and paprika for 1 minute, then tip into the slow cooker.
Add the carrots, tomatoes, beans, purée and stock. Stir and season.
Cover and cook on low for 8–9 hours while you're at work. If your slow cooker has a timer, set it to switch to 'keep warm' when it finishes.
Make the mash (or heat a pouch) when you're ready to eat.
Serve half over the mash. Let the rest cool for up to an hour, then put it in a covered tub in the fridge for Thursday.
recipe.tip: Chop the onion and carrots tonight and keep them in the fridge, so the morning is just browning and tipping in.

2026-11-04.note: Hockey Academy night 6:15–7:45pm (The Lindum). One pan, about 20 minutes.

ingredients: 300g raw king prawns (frozen is fine, defrosted)
300g cherry tomatoes, halved (or a 400g tin chopped tomatoes)
2 tbsp cream cheese, or a splash of cream
Grated parmesan, and a squeeze of lemon if you have one, to serve
steps: Soften the onion in the oil in a wide pan for 5 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the orzo and tomatoes and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock, bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes, stirring often so it doesn't stick, until the orzo is almost tender. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Stir in the prawns and cook for 3–4 minutes until they're pink all the way through.
Stir in the cream cheese and spinach until the spinach wilts. Season.
Serve with parmesan and a squeeze of lemon.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: scoop hers out before the lemon and cut the prawns into small pieces. Defrost frozen prawns in the fridge from the morning, or in a bowl of cold water for 20 minutes.

2026-11-05.meal: Sausage & bean casserole leftovers with mash (from Tuesday)
2026-11-05.note: Bonfire night, out to watch the fireworks. Tuesday's saved half for Jess and Frank, reheated in 10 minutes. Put some in a flask to take with you if you like.

ingredients: Mash (fresh potatoes or a microwave pouch) or crusty bread
steps: Tip the casserole into a pan with a splash of water.
Heat gently for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until it's piping hot all the way through. Or microwave in a covered bowl for 4–5 minutes, stirring halfway.
Heat the mash or butter some bread while it warms.
Serve, and fill a warmed flask with any extra to take to the fireworks.
recipe.tip: Only reheat it once. Warm the flask with boiling water first so it stays hot.
